provenance.coverage: Integrated end-to-end behavior for all 8 plan requirements, 2 preservation checks and a requirement-retention/defect ledger (closed vocabulary, exact set).
provenance.derivation: Private T012 realtime push-to-talk slice (plan #246, stacked layer PRs landing as one merge, a cross-layer repair) re-synthesized as a sanitized TypeScript stand-in: a canonical protocol plus three parallel layer outputs carrying realistic cross-layer integration defects (renamed handshake field, protocol version skew, a requirement dropped by a mis-split brief, content leaking into telemetry, a seconds/milliseconds mismatch). No private code, providers, hostnames or credentials are included. v2 (MB-010c follow-up, live evidence): the exact-five ledger check rejected a genuine, fixed memory leak (Sonnet) while correctly rejecting a nonexistent auth bypass (MAI). An independent audit of the landed base (audited_base_defects) found exactly one genuine defect beyond the five integration defects. The ledger now requires the five, admits only audited extras, rejects nonexistent/unknown/duplicate categories, and verifies a claimed leak fix behaviorally; the reference also fixes and lists the leak. Live v1 evidence: benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MB-010r-orchestrate-voice-integration-v1-outcomes.json (sha256 c7781661a9d3ec72bca2edcc1bf7fe0e5736713d87d72fcd654a19d58b77e008). v3: trusted native behavior diagnostics (benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MB-010r-orchestrate-v2-ledger-diagnostics.json, sha256 c049c7b4893772309b0244b4431852403562308b7ba9b529e15874fb7de83d90) reproduced a re-entrant cancel-ordering defect (a cancel processed during respond() is followed by a response). It joins the audited genuine set as race-condition with a behavioral fix check; a rejected re-join leaves the original session unchanged, so auth-bypass stays audited absent. The reference fixes and lists it. v4: native v3 admission and live outcomes (benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MB-010r-orchestrate-v3-outcomes.json, sha256 1aa97a50ca3c5076674c3b9fb5ff72e1e9b6c672cb12c27e1ce7f4f11edf6cce) found literal overspecification. R1 required sessionId 's1' though the plan says ids are opaque; it is now an opaque-id check (non-empty string, stable for the session on the wire, client and telemetry, distinct across concurrent sessions, later frames accepted). Scenarios observe protocol frames instead of unspecified telemetry event names; R4 checks the response produced from the turn's transcript instead of a transcript-length literal, and that audio carries the turn's correlation id; R6 and pre-join/unparsable rejection are frame-presence checks, not exact frame lists; the memory-leak check measures retention growth with ended sessions instead of total collection size; the ledger checks every plan-table layer mapping and that defect files exist and locate the defect. The instruction now states the preserved pre-join, unparsable-frame and out-of-order behavior, that scratch self-tests are ungraded, and what defect files mean. Extra defects (memory-leak, race-condition) remain optional but must be genuine and fixed when listed, by design.
